title: Charlotte Jackson Fine Art presents Still Friends After All These Years
summary: Charlotte Jackson Fine Art will present a group exhibition of work by three artists Still Friends After All These Years. The show will run from September 11 to October 10, with an Opening reception with the artists on Friday, September 11 from 5-7 p.m. On Saturday, September 12 from 2-4 p.m. there will be a Gallery Talk: A Conversation with Charles Arnoldi, Ron Cooper, Laddie John Dill and Rani Singh. The gallery is located in the Railyard Arts District at 554 South Guadalupe Street. The colors sink deep into you. The heat of a gouache red. The radiant blue glow of light in a glass tube. The shimmering gold of pearlescent pigment on Plexiglas. The forms and formats as distinct as the techniques. Yet these works of art, large and small, all somehow find their way deep into the body of the viewer - shifting, shaping, answering questions we hadn't realized needed asking.

title: Milestone's Sept. 26 Premier Military & Edged Weapons Auction spans 250 years of historic battles
summary: On September 26, Milestone Auctions will present the Fall 2026 edition of its Premier Military & Edged Weapons Sale, an event that’s always a favorite with specialist collectors. The fully-curated 627-lot selection of rare, well-provenanced antique and vintage items is designed to take military buffs on a journey steeped in American and world history. The 250-year timeline starts in the 18th century with coveted Revolutionary War items and progresses to the modern-war era. title: Artemis Fine Arts and Arte Primitivo join forces for two-day auction of ancient art and antiquities
summary: Artemis Fine Arts and Arte Primitivo are bringing their expertise together for a two-day auction on September 15 and 16, 2026, offering a wide-ranging selection of Pre-Columbian, Native American, fossil, Egyptian, Greek, Roman, Near Eastern, African, Tribal and Asian material. The sale opens with Pre-Columbian, Native American and fossil works on September 15, followed the next day by antiquities and works from Africa and Asia. Among the most striking works on the first day is a Teotihuacan ceremonial mask carved from obsidian, dating to around 450–650 CE. With its broad brow, heavy-lidded eyes and idealized features, the mask belongs to a type long associated with ritual and funerary contexts. title: Roy Lichtenstein personal collection coming to Sotheby's across two October sales
summary: This October, Sotheby’s will present an offering of works emerging from the personal collection of Dorothy and Roy Lichtenstein, showcasing five decades of artistic output from the Pop art icon. Bringing together paintings, drawings, collages, sculptures, ephemera, prints, and editions, the group offers a broad exploration of Lichtenstein’s practice. This particular selection gives an in-depth look into Lichtenstein’s process and the development of his ideas through various media, showcasing the full range of the artist’s creative process. Taken together, the works capture the retrospective spirit of the Collection and reflect both the range and consistency of Lichtenstein’s vision across multiple mediums and throughout his oeuvre. title: Gagosian Beverly Hills hosts Jia Aili's first West Coast solo exhibition
summary: Gagosian announces Seeing Through: Jia Aili’s Parallel Paintings, a major exhibition of new works by the artist. This is Jia’s first solo presentation at the gallery in Beverly Hills and marks his first solo project with Gagosian since 2019’s Combustion in New York. A key figure in Chinese contemporary painting, Jia crafts expansive, dynamic compositions that engage with classic art historical modes. Challenging established visual conventions in the context of a rapidly changing world, he responds directly to the fluid nature of contemporary experience. In these canvases, natural landscapes, historical images, and abstract forms intertwine as the artist reconfigures source material from disparate periods and cultures to build a complex, layered reality that resists any singular narrative. title: New Los Angeles exhibition explores John Baldessari's three-dimensional and spatial works
summary: John Baldessari is renowned for his brilliant visual experiments with language, photography, and painting spanning from the 1960s to 2020. Less explored is the artist’s creative use of three-dimensional space, whether by deploying patterned wallpapers, working in bas-relief, or creating captivating sculptures and installations. Sprüth Magers is pleased to present an exhibition at the Los Angeles gallery devoted to the sculptural impulse in Baldessari’s work, featuring projects that have been brought together for the first time to explore how the artist played with space and scale to dramatic effect. Already in the 1980s, the artist expanded the physical bounds of his two-dimensional practice with his composite photoworks, in which multiple framed elements spread imagery in configurations across the gallery walls. title: Sotheby's to auction Princess Diana's iconic 'Revenge Dress' in New York
summary: On the warm summer evening of June 29, 1994, Diana, Princess of Wales, made a showstopping arrival at Serpentine, one of London’s most famous art galleries, for a fundraising dinner hosted by Vanity Fair. As she stepped out of her car into a blaze of camera flashes from a crowd of photographers, she was wearing a striking figure-hugging, strapless black silk evening dress by Greek designer Christina Stambolian accessorised with a royal jewel, a black clutch and black pumps. Beamed to the world within minutes, the look would become one of the most enduring fashion statements of the 20th century. Now, more than three decades later, that very dress returns to the spotlight. title: Christie's to offer Belgian collector Mia Van Hool's contemporary art collection
summary: Christie's announces the forthcoming sale on December 2 of Mia Van Hool: L'audace à l'oeuvre, which will be exhibited in Brussels from September 10 to 13 as part of RendezVous Brussels Art Week. Organized in honor of Mia Van Hool, a leading figure of the Belgian contemporary art scene renowned for her discerning eye, this sale also provides Christie's with an opportunity to celebrate 50 years of active presence at the heart of one of Europe's most inventive cultural capitals and to reaffirm its commitment to Belgium. title: Qatar Museums announces permanent pavilion for Gerhard Richter
summary: Qatar Museums today announced the creation of Doha Pavilion: Gerhard Richter, a new permanent, site-specific structure conceived by the world-renowned artist. Doha Pavilion has been designed by Gerhard Richter as a free-standing work of art and architecture housing a distinct body of his paintings and sculpture. Selldorf Architects worked with the artist to realise his vision for the project, which will be located in Doha’s MIA Park, the expansive public space outside the Museum of Islamic Art. Doha Pavilion will be unveiled on 20 November 2026 on the eve of the opening of Rubaiya Qatar, the nation’s new contemporary art quadrennial. Her Excellency Sheikha Al Mayassa bint Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, Chairperson of Qatar Museums said, “Qatar’s ambitious programme of public art installations has been developed through our relationships with outstanding figures in contemporary art. title: Sotheby's unveils highlights from Magnificent Judaica sale
summary: Sotheby's today unveiled highlights from Magnificent Judaica, a live auction in New York on December 17, 2026. Anchored by an exceptional group of medieval and Renaissance Hebrew manuscripts from a distinguished collection, the sale brings together works that illuminate the artistic, intellectual, and religious life of Jewish communities across Europe over the course of several centuries. Additional highlights include important examples of Judaica silver, among them works associated with the Rothschild family and one of the smallest known Torah scrolls in existence. Additional property from the sale will be announced later this season. Leading the sale is an illustrated mahzor created in Italy circa 1475 by Joel ben Simeon, one of the few named Jewish artists of the medieval period. title: Christie's announces December sale of historic JPHY Buddhist art collection in Paris
summary: Christie's announced the sale of the JPHY Collection, comprising a live auction in Paris on 10 December, Masterpieces of Buddhist Art: Peaceful and Wrathful, and an online sale, Indian, Himalayan, and Southeast Asian Art, open for bidding from 30 November to 11 December. Representing the finest collection of Indian and Himalayan Buddhist art to be offered on the international market in more than a decade, the JPHY Collection marks a landmark event for the global art market. This is particularly true in Paris, where the JPHY Collection is set to rank among the French capital's most important collection sales of the autumn season, in a category where ensembles of this scale are exceptionally rare. title: 2026 David and Yuko Juda Art Foundation Grant winner announced
summary: The judges' decision was announced at a special reception on 10 September at Annely Juda Fine Art's new gallery, 16 Hanover Square, Mayfair. The grant gives the recipient £50,000 to help alleviate some of their financial pressures and give them freedom to concentrate on their practice. The winner of this year's grant is Soheila Sokhanvari (b.1964), an artist whose practice explores memory, identity and cultural displacement through painting, drawing and installation. Trained initially in biochemistry before turning to fine art, Sokhanvari employs the traditional technique of egg tempera on calf vellum, painstakingly grinding her own pigments to create works that evoke the precision of illuminated manuscripts. Drawing on magic realism, symbolism and allegory, her work addresses political and social histories through metaphor, resisting fixed or authoritarian narratives. title: Rabkin Foundation awards $400,000 to eight visual arts journalists
summary: Marking a decade of support for arts writers, the Rabkin Foundation has named its 2026 recipients of the Rabkin Prize, awarding eight visual arts journalists $50,000 each in recognition of their creative and intellectual contributions to the field. The 2026 Rabkin Prize winners are: Damien Davis, an artist, educator, and writer whose work explores how power, race, and cultural narratives are constructed and circulated; Melaine Ferdinand-King, a cultural strategist, poet, and writer focused on historical and community narratives, and the inaugural curator of the African American Museum of Rhode Island; Tyler Green, a critic, author, and longtime host of The Modern Art Notes Podcast; Alicia Inez Guzmán, a critic and award-winning investigative journalist focused on culture and land use; Julia Halperin, a critic, editor, investigative data journalist, and co-founder of the Burns Halperin Report, which tracks equity and

title: Sotheby's unveils full auction line-up for Nightcap, following record first half for Wine & Spirits
summary: Today, Sotheby’s unveils the full auction programme for Nightcap, its new global Wine & Spirits Festival, bringing together world-class wines and spirits, collecting opportunities, tastings, dinners and culture at Sotheby’s iconic Breuer building in New York. Taking place 16–19 September, Nightcap will present one of the most significant wine and spirits auction programmes ever staged in New York, with more than $10 million of exceptional wines and spirits offered across five dedicated auctions, alongside a curated programme of experiences for leading collectors, producers and enthusiasts. Admission to Nightcap auctions is free and open to all. title: Capitain Petzel presents Austin Martin White's second solo exhibition in Berlin
summary: Capitain Petzel announces The lie, the larp and the lusophile, Austin Martin White’s second solo exhibition with the gallery, spanning its entire exhibition space. Through paintings and works on paper, White investigates the construction of historical memory, exploring postcolonial histories and the ways images shape cultural narratives while addressing the unstable boundary between historical fact, national myth, and cultural identity. At the core of the exhibition is the legacy of the Brazilian Baroque sculptor Antônio Francisco Lisboa (c. 1738–1814), known as Aleijadinho, whose biography has long oscillated between documented history and legend. White presents portraits of the artist alongside depictions of his prophet sculptures at the Sanctuary of Bom Jesus de Matosinhos in Congonhas. title: Christie's presents its Hong Kong Annual Sale of Indian, Himalayan and Southeast Asian Art
summary: Christie’s announces the highlights of its Hong Kong annual sale of Indian, Himalayan and Southeast Asian Art, to be held live on 30 October 2026 during Hong Kong Asian Art Week. Bringing together a selection of rare and fresh-to-market masterpieces and important single-owner collections, the auction features works of remarkable quality and provenance, reflecting the growing appeal of the category among collectors across Asia and around the world. Leading the sale is an exceptional Green Schist Gable Relief (image above), dating to the 2nd/3rd century and ranking among the finest and most complete narrative reliefs of its kind remaining in private hands. title: Kumu Art Museum presents its fall 2026 programme focusing on Sámi and Finno-Ugric Images
summary: This autumn, Kumu Art Museum opens two parallel exhibitions focusing on Sámi activist art and the role of Finno-Ugric ethnography in Estonian nation-building. Developed through three years of dialogue, they share a concern with the close connections between power, images, and knowledge production. Sámi art started to become politicized in the 1970s, when many artists joined the struggle for Indigenous rights. By comparison, the opportunities for the small Finno-Ugric nations living in Russia to stand up for their rights have been radically more constrained, especially since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. title: Francisco Carolinum Linz presents first institutional retrospective of Ana María Caballero
summary: The Francisco Carolinum Linz presents Read the Room, the first institutional mid-career retrospective of the artist and poet Ana María Caballero. The exhibition brings together key works from the fields of installation art, performance art, sculpture, choreography, cinematic art and literature. Together, these works offer insight into Caballero's artistic practice, which is based on the fundamental belief that language is not a fixed medium, but a living process that unfolds through the interplay of writing and reading. The exhibition's starting point is Fifty Ways of Looking at a Poem. For this project, Caballero invited 50 people to read and annotate the same poem. Each edition documents an individual reading process, revealing how meaning emerges, changes and multiplies through engagement with a text. title: Berlin exhibition asks what comes between destruction and reconstruction
summary: Rebuilding a city is rarely as simple as replacing what has been destroyed. Behind damaged walls and shattered neighborhoods lie disrupted communities, erased histories, contested land and memories that cannot be reconstructed with concrete alone. A new exhibition at the Akademie der Künste in Berlin takes that difficult space as its subject. Metaxy: Between Destruction and Reconstruction, on view from September 10 through December 6, 2026, brings together artists, architects and spatial practitioners to examine what happens between catastrophe and rebuilding—and why decisions made during that interval can determine what kind of future eventually takes shape. The title comes from the ancient Greek word metaxy, meaning “between.” Here, the term describes a space in which societies confront the past while negotiating the future,

title: Galerie Nathalie Obadia presents solo exhibition by Robert Kushner in Paris
summary: Galerie Nathalie Obadia is presenting a new solo exhibition by American artist Robert Kushner in Paris. Bringing together twelve works produced between 2019 and 2025-eleven works on Japanese paper and one painting on canvas- the exhibition unveils a recent body of work in which the botanical world intertwines with ornament. Cradled in gold leaf and expanses of colour, stems, leaves and petals unfurl. Through these works, Robert Kushner offers an attentive vision of the forms of nature, in which beauty is not a mere embellishment, but a way of contemplating the world. Born in California in 1949, Robert Kushner was one of the founders of the Pattern and Decoration movement, which emerged in the United States in the 1970s in reaction to Minimalism and Conceptual art. title: Juan Asensio explores nature and geometry in new Madrid sculpture show
summary: Galería Elvira González, opens APENAS TRANSITAR (Barely Passing Through), the eleventh solo exhibition by sculptor Juan Asensio (Cuenca, 1959) at the gallery. The show features 20 sculptures and continues the path begun in his two previous exhibitions, Verba naturae and Contra natura, in which the artist examines the relationship between nature and geometry. Asensio describes himself as essentially a rational person, and geometric order is the central axis of his work. His interest in nature stems from this: the need to understand how the world is constructed and to uncover the patterns that pulse beneath all things. Over the years, that trajectory has gradually reversed. title: Full contents of historic ex-cellar auction of Château Haut-Brion are revealed
summary: Earlier this summer, Sotheby’s and Domaine Clarence Dillon shared the news that they would stage a momentous auction of wines sourced exclusively and directly from the legendary cellars of Château Haut-Brion, in celebration of ninety years of Dillon family stewardship. Those nine decades make the Dillon family the second-longest dynasty to have cared for these vines across six centuries of recorded ownership. Today, as the complete catalogue for the sale goes live on Sotheby’s website, the full scope of wines and bespoke experiences which together constitute this landmark offering is now revealed. Château Haut-Brion, Domaine Clarence Dillon, Celebrating our 10th Decade of Family Stewardship brings together the full breadth of the estate’s production. title: New book reexamines ritual violence and sacrifice in ancient Mesoamerica
summary: A new English-language volume is bringing together some of the latest archaeological research on ritual violence, human sacrifice and ceremonial treatment of the body in ancient Mesoamerica, combining new scientific methods with an effort to understand these practices within the belief systems of the societies that carried them out. Ritual Violence and Related Body Treatments in Ancient Mesoamerica, published by British Archaeological Reports, was recently presented at Mexico’s National Museum of Anthropology. Edited by archaeologist Vera Tiesler, the book gathers contributions from 36 researchers working across a wide range of disciplines and institutions, including Mexico’s National Institute of Anthropology and History. title: Ancient Olmec offerings from El Manatí reunited for landmark exhibition in Xalapa
summary: Nearly four decades after one of the most extraordinary discoveries in Mesoamerican archaeology, objects recovered from the sacred Olmec site of Cerro El Manatí are being brought together again in a major exhibition at the Xalapa Museum of Anthropology. Lords of Water, Olmec Sacred Spaces, opening September 10, 2026, presents 90 archaeological objects from El Manatí alongside material from the related sites of La Merced and El Macayal. Organized by the INAH Veracruz Center and Universidad Veracruzana, the exhibition will remain on view for a year as part of the museum’s 70th-anniversary celebrations.
